profile.headline: Product Engineer
profile.summary:
I grew up on the Internet and for over 20 years have contributed to dozens (or hundreds?) of websites and web apps as a designer and developer. These projects have spanned my freelance, open source, agency, and startup experience. Most recently I have worked in fintech, growing along with Vestwell on its journey from seed stage to a Series E company with a clear path to profitability.

Along the way I have developed my taste for and ability to execute quality software both individually and as part of a team in various roles. Cross-disciplinary experience and honed instincts help me move fast and get things done to a high standard. Beyond this I have contributed to processes, tools, documentation, and one-on-one mentoring that enable teams to do the same.

I am currently seeking product design and UI engineering opportunities that leverage my combined design and development experience.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Contributed to an internal sub-accounting solution built with a microservices approach using AWS Lambda, EventBridge, and Step Functions via the Serverless framework

• Implemented structured logs for multiple Serverless projects and helped to integrate them and APM instrumentation data with Elasticsearch

• Advocated for structured logs, designed their format, and implemented a trial within a key public Node.js service with ingestion into Sumo Logic

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description:
• Joined full-time to focus on furthering the Vestwell user experience while scaling to 200+ employees and nearly one million savers (retirement plan participants) employed by 25,000+ small businesses across the country

• Lead a gradual transition from a proprietary server-rendered React architecture to a modern, responsive single page app following a hybrid "islands" approach building various tooling and methods to mount and hydrate components in the browser. 

• Helped to scale frontend development 3x through implementation of a monorepo, code linting, code formatting, exception monitoring with Sentry, and automated versioning while simplifying the architecture to align with industry norms

• Collaborated with the company's first full-time designer to expand the component library and establish a broader design system implemented in Sketch and React and aligned to company's first brand guidelines.

• Iterated the design system through regular product/design collaboration using Figma and Chromatic/Storybook. Helped deliver improvements to user satisfaction and retention, achieve WCAG 2.0 accessibility conformance, and executed a second rebrand.

• Served as tech lead of a Scrum squad (1 PM, 1 QA, 3 full stack engineers) for 2 years (half remote) focused primarily on advisor and saver-facing features. Worked closely with product management and designers to plan and deliver our roadmap.

• Closely collaborated with Scala engineers to design and deliver next generation REST API endpoints and enforce their consistency through OpenAPI contracts and the JSON:API specification with a style guide implemented via OpenAPI linting rules and documentation generated using ReDoc

• Contributed to the UI and architecture of various key features including dashboards, investment elections, advisor reporting, payroll contribution processing, company registration, whitelabeling, and more

positions.title: Frontend Developer
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States
positions.description:
• Filled a frontend development gap in seed stage early days, shipping MVP capabilities as quickly as possible with few resources while establishing an early component library and other patterns along the way

• Oversaw frontend contributions from a mix of junior and contract engineers, mentoring to ensure code quality

positions.title: Svelte System
positions.description:
Svelte is a competitor to React that is notable in everything it can do that React does, but with less code to write and better, compiled code that is fast and energy efficient. React’s strength is increasingly the ecosystem that has built around it.

Two projects within that, Styled System and Chakra UI, inspired me to implement a similar means of styling Svelte components within the constraints of a design system expressed as configuration. Unlike the React-based inspiration, Svelte System components maintain Svelte’s efficiency with zero runtime.

positions.title: Dash Marshall v3
positions.description:
Revisiting a site I originally built in 2015, the architecture and urban strategy practice had leveled up in Brooklyn while also expanding to Detroit. A growing body of work was becoming increasingly untenable to maintain as a static site deployed from the laptop of partner Bryan Boyer. 

I rebuilt the site using Next.js and the Sanity CMS, enabling the entire team to contribute to an ongoing database of projects. The site still benefits from server-rendered pages but now uses modern on-demand incremental static regeneration to update the site quickly whenever content is published.

positions.title: People Party!
positions.description:
A collaboration with Dash Marshall, this is a tool for creating architectural renderings that are representative of local demographics. We built a MVP beta that, with the press of a key, generates a dynamic population of people — plus some pups! — of all ages, shapes, sizes, skin colors, and individual styles.

To save time and money an offline-first strategy was used, persisting data using IndexedDB and managing state with Redux Toolkit. Further time was saved using the MUI component library and the RedwoodJS framework.
positions.insights: Skills: IndexedDB · Interaction Design · React.js · Figma · Redwood · CSS · Redux · JavaScript · Node.js

positions.title: Autonomous Vehicles: Future Scenarios
positions.description:
An extension of the Global Atlas effort with further support from the National League of Cities, this microsite presents four scenarios of how autonomous vehicles could improve everyday life. Each is a richly illustrated story told through a journalistic lens and backend by extensive research conducted for the Global Atlas and a related print publication.

Built as a sister site to the Global Atlas, it co-exists and shares some code with that effort in a monorepo. React was again leveraged, this time for its ability to seamlessly weave content, illustration, and interactive features together through the abstraction of components. Content is sourced from Markdown files and rendered with React using ReMark tooling. Animations were implemented using the GreenSock library.
positions.insights: Skills: React.js · CSS · JavaScript · Node.js · GreenSock Animation Platform (GSAP)

positions.title: Ten Thousand
positions.description:
This project began closely collaborating with the founding team on a custom Shopify theme for the initial beta launch of Ten Thousand’s direct-to-consumer line of highly customizable, minimalist, sustainably-made sports apparel.

The success of the beta lead to an expansive v2 redesign with an early use of React on top of Shopify that enabled a premium shopping experience. Other technologies such as Imgix, Redux, and a Gulp-driven SVG workflow were incorporated to further extend what Shopify could do at the time.

Later, I built a custom solution for product trials requiring deferred transactions using AWS Lambda, Stripe, and the Shopify API.

positions.title: Designer / Developer
positions.description: After returning to New York I started my own design and development studio working independently and with small teams on a variety of projects.

positions.title: Sparkart
positions.description:
I continued working with Sparkart in a freelance capacity to see-through migration from and shutdown of the Clique Tools platform I helped create.

Following this effort I also worked together with a small team of engineers on projects supporting Sparkart’s angel investments including Space Tango, Toymail, the Trnio 3D scanner, and an internal tool to identify and collect evidence of counterfeit Amazon Marketplace products.

positions.title: Global Atlas of Autonomous Vehicles in Cities
positions.description: Sponsored by Bloomberg Philanthropies, this website presented the results of the first ever global survey of what cities are doing to prepare for AVs. I used React, Mapbox and various custom tools to generate static pages from content defined in CSV and YAML files that the survey team, a joint venture of Dash Marshall and Star City Group, could update via GitHub and self-service deploy via CircleCI.

positions.title: The Infatuation
positions.description: Developed static microsites for various brand partnerships, a personalized restaurant recommendation app, and the first ever EEEEEATSCON in Los Angeles.

positions.title: Dash Marshall
positions.description:
Since working out of their far too short-lived Makeshift Society space in Williamsburg I have collaborated with this small architecture and urban strategy practice on a number of projects. The first was their own website, designed by Two Points.

In response to a requirement to avoid dependencies and maintenance burdens I created a static site generated from Markdown content in a Dropbox folder. Markdown was extended with custom syntaxes and frontmatter to enable various layout possibilities. A workflow to incrementally generate responsive images and deploy them was also created.

positions.title: Chief Product Officer
positions.description:
• Managed development of two projects that replaced Storyteller and narrowed our focus by extracting it's API proxy and shifting site development to the early (0.x) Node.js ecosystem emerging at the time. We built an open source framework called Solidus that is still in use.

• Helped implement CI/CD for Solidus projects, initially using Modulus with CircleCI and later Heroku

• Managed development of a new platform built to meet the unique needs of the business unmet by anything else on the market. It is focused on selling memberships offering access to exclusive content, events, and packages of merchandise.

• Defined a migration strategy and oversaw efforts to move remaining properties from Clique Tools to the new solution, porting it’s widget abstraction to Handlebars helpers

• Completed adoption of AWS and shutdown of legacy data center servers with the support of a consultant

• Implemented Single Sign On (SSO) to address access complexity resulting from the growing number of third-party services in use. Initially using Okta and later Google Cloud Identity (formerly Bitium).

• Implemented a data warehouse solution to integrate internal and Shopify data and generate unified reports to clients using RJMetrics (later acquired by Magento and Adobe)

positions.title: Product Manager
positions.description:
• Worked closely with the internal engineering team to deliver improvements to Clique Tools that included an interactive IDE, git-based version control, and WYSIWYG email editing

• Advocated for a new API-driven approach to development to reduce the company’s software footprint and enable focus on the unique aspects of the business

• Collaborated with the engineering team to realize the vision in the form of Storyteller: an integrated API catalog, proxy, and IDE for creating websites with content from a mix of internal and third-party services. The platform was used in production for America's Cup and UFC. We also seriously explored productization. 

• Implemented content management for America’s Cup with an early use of WordPress in a headless capacity

positions.title: UX Team Lead
positions.description:
• Oversaw dozens of web site design and development projects, often delivered on 2 week turnarounds

• Built up a team of several designers and taught them to code, enabling a hybrid approach that was more efficient and yielded results that pushed the boundaries of what was possible with CSS at the time — despite Internet Explorer 6!

• Implemented asset management, a testing lab, and resources for  creating design materials by hand

• Managed the design and frontend development of a custom ecommerce platform for Metropark that ultimately delivered revenue eclipsing it’s chain of unique lifestyle retail stores.

• Worked with an internal team of engineers to execute the Metropark backend in an early (pre-1.0) use of Rails and contributed to it’s CMS and operational tooling
  
• Helped conceive, design, and build Clique Tools: an internal platform expanding on what we did for Metropark to deliver integrated content, ecommerce, social networking, and marketing capabilities to all of the agency’s clients. Over 300 websites, 1 million accounts, and millions in revenue were produced over its lifetime. 

• Contributed to art direction for a diverse mix of entertainment and adjacent industry clients including Linkin Park, The Killers, Bon Jovi, Criss Angel, Tim McGraw, and UFC

• Personally designed an iteration of bonjovi.com and it's fan club, live throughout the 2010 The Circle tour, highest grossing in the US for the year

positions.title: Dot-com Prospector
positions.description:
My years in high school happened to coincide with the web 1.0 dot-com boom. I was able to translate earlier tinkering with computers and BBS systems into income by designing and building websites for local businesses.

From my bedroom in Virginia I was also able to connect with people around the world via IRC, participating in the digital art scene creating ASCII, ANSI, and "hirez" artwork. I was also active in the BeOS community, contributing to the BeNews website and helped test Táve Imagination, an Adobe-style creative tool. The logo I created for Táve is still used by an iteration of the brand, now owned by Foreground.

IRC and the art scene also lead to my connecting with Naveen Jain and his nascent agency called Sparkart. I worked as a contractor starting in high school and throughout my time at SVA, building websites for every notable nü-metal band at the time that started with a chance opportunity for Linkin Park. After art school I moved to Oakland and joined full-time.
positions.insights: Skills: Interaction Design · User Interface Design · CSS · User Experience · Adobe Photoshop

experience.title: Dot-com Prospector
experience.description:
My years in high school happened to coincide with the web 1.0 dot-com boom. I was able to translate earlier tinkering with computers and BBS systems into income by designing and building websites for local businesses.

From my bedroom in Virginia I was also able to connect with people around the world via IRC, participating in the digital art scene creating ASCII, ANSI, and "hirez" artwork. I was also active in the BeOS community, contributing to the BeNews website and helped test Táve Imagination, an Adobe-style creative tool. The logo I created for Táve is still used by an iteration of the brand, now owned by Foreground.

IRC and the art scene also lead to my connecting with Naveen Jain and his nascent agency called Sparkart. I worked as a contractor starting in high school and throughout my time at SVA, building websites for every notable nü-metal band at the time that started with a chance opportunity for Linkin Park. After art school I moved to Oakland and joined full-time.
